scores.why: A provides the clearest environment, access and proof-deployment plan with sign-off artifacts, B and C cover the basic setup with limited environment or pipeline detail, and D offers a short setup promise diluted by unrelated monthly support.

A and B offer equivalent component mapping, template construction and stage testing, C substitutes author training for a site-building method, and D adds useful content inventory and template policies but leaves its editor compatibility and promised pilot execution unclear.

A and D provide credible deployment, testing and rollback controls but thin search protection, B gives a partial cutover sequence without accountable outputs or effort, and C adds the strongest URL mapping, automated redirect checks and post-launch crawl while still leaving some indexing controls unspecified.

A offers no training method, B directly tests independent page creation and publication with practical workshops and launch support, and C and D provide useful role-based practice and guides but concentrate on editing without demonstrating publishing readiness.

A and B provide generic shared-identifier schema design and source reconciliation, C substantially improves source mapping and acceptance through Snowflake sales totals and identifier checks, and D diverts into unrequested audience publishing while barely describing preparation of the requested data.

A usefully measures loyalty-ID coverage but promises stitching and data views without explaining their configuration, B offers only a brief configuration commitment, C adds an identity plan and sample stitching checks, and D most completely includes data-view construction and metric reconciliation although its stitching design remains generic.

A outlines a plausible warehouse ingestion path but adds unrelated sources and lacks validation or scheduling accountability, B and C add equivalent inventories and match-rate checks while leaving reconciliation mostly promised, and D gives the most complete Snowflake-specific access, mapping, data-view and validation sequence.

A and D describe competent but generic Workspace delivery with optional executive scorecards, B connects concrete marketing and merchandising questions to KPIs, Snowflake reconciliation and user acceptance, and C offers little beyond building unspecified agreed projects.

A most clearly scopes Power BI executive dashboards, owners, permissions and effort, B and C provide equivalent BI-extension setup and reconciliation but dilute the Power BI focus with other tools, and D supplies the basic connection route and checks without a dashboard delivery plan or accountable effort.

A provides a sound role-based Workspace training plan, B weakens similar coverage with an unsupported separate Adobe Analytics license dependency, C gives only a high-level promise, and D adds tailored exercises and readiness checks but retains that license dependency and leaves its governance-label behavior needing confirmation.

A explains CTA clicks but omits page-view implementation and adds irrelevant stitching licensing, B states the full collection route but gives little operational detail, C improves setup, field specification and delivery accountability while leaving collection-rule configuration implicit, and D adds a page measurement plan to concrete click validation but still omits the actual page-view rule and Web SDK routing setup.

A answers go-live rather than monthly support, B provides the strongest release planning, regression testing and operational reporting cycle, and C and D offer equivalent basic releases and log reviews with clear monthly effort but limited incident-response or service-level detail.

A and B provide equivalent monthly journey analysis, readouts and owned follow-up actions, C strengthens the service with retail journey examples, success measures and data-completeness checks, and D supplies only a general recurring analysis promise without scope, deliverables or effort.

notes: Materially equivalent implementations receive equal scores despite changes in introductory prose, formatting or planning estimates.
The strongest answers turn Tallgrass-specific web, store and loyalty needs into concrete implementation steps, validation and accountable deliverables rather than merely repeating client facts.
Promised outputs do not compensate fully for omitted methods, especially for stitching, data views, page-view collection and independent publication.
Unrequested audience activation and unsupported separate Adobe Analytics licensing reduce fit; unrelated channel, BI-tool and mobile examples add little to the requested scope.

Product-specific claims that cannot be established from the permitted text remain uncertainties rather than asserted errors, including editor compatibility, package entitlements and governance behavior.
